newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil called $1-$2 up, Brent 5-10 cts higher.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil called $1-$2 up, Brent 5-10 cts higher.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were called to open between $1.00 and $2.00 a tonne higher on Friday, in a follow-through to Thursday's sharp rally.
May gas oil closed $1.50 a tonne higher on Thursday at $169.00.
June Brent was expected to open some five to ten cents up after Thursday's 53 cents gains took the contract to $18.67 a barrel.
"It's got the bit between the teeth now...we're looking for a continuation of yesterday," a broker said.
Brent was untraded on Singapore's SIMEX but the bid/ask range moved up to $18.68/$18.80 a barrel. July Brent traded 11 cents up on SIMEX at $18.75.
Gains were also seen on ACCESS, with unleaded gasoline futures, which spearheaded Thursday's ascent, gaining 1.73 cents a gallon to 62.65 cents.
Signs that U.S. gasoline was firming of ahead of expected strong demand for the Memorial Day weekend sparked a strong technical rally across the oil products complex.
And drop in temperatures in the U.S. Northeast forecast for this weekend combined with heavy Far East buying.
Strong demand, particularly into Indonesia and China, could lend particular support to gas oil, brokers Credit Lyonnais Rouse said in a daily report.
But some brokers said that the market's bearish underlying tone could eat into recent gains.

The International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday that world oil supply grew by some 300,000 barrels per day (bpd) in April thanks mainly to rising OPEC output of 220,000 bpd. But demand for OPEC barrels is set to remain stagnant, the energy watchdog said.
